faqs.q: Groundhogs keep burrowing around my Harrisonburg home — can they be removed?
faqs.a: Yes. The woodchuck, or groundhog, is a designated nuisance species in Virginia and also counts as a higher-risk rabies species in raccoon-variant areas, so burrows against a foundation, slab, or barn in Harrisonburg are worth acting on before the tunnel system undermines concrete. Our crew handles groundhogs at the property under permit — Virginia does not allow trap-and-relocate — and advises on fencing and harbor removal so the burrow stays empty.

Harrisonburg.wildlife_intro:
Harrisonburg is Rockingham County's city — a university and farm-service center in the central Valley in Harrisonburg. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: black's Run through downtown, James Madison University, Massanutten's slopes east of the city. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Harrisonburg — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
